subject: Aurora MAP & commercial proposal / evaluation timeline
messages:

Subject: Aurora MAP & evaluation timeline - draft

Hi Sarah —

Great to connect last week. Attached is a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lines up the evaluation milestones we discussed and the commercial checkpoints tied to each milestone. High level:

- Week 1–2: Pilot kick-off (data ingestion + quickstart).
- Week 3–6: Evaluation window (latency/cost/accuracy benchmarks).
- Week 7–10: Pilot scaling + production readiness (throughput, autoscale test).
- Week 12: Commit decision / PO issuance.

Commercially, we propose a two-stage approach: an evaluation credit to cover pilot costs, then a first-year committed usage with a ramp schedule and a renewal uplift clause that adjusts unit pricing based on committed throughput at renewal. Details are in the MAP appendix.

Ask: please review the milestones and let me know if the dates below work for you. If you can confirm target PO timing and whether Aurora prefers annual or quarterly invoicing, I’ll send a commercial term sheet tied to the MAP.

Attachments: Aurora_MAP_v1.pdf (draft MAP)

Thanks —
Rishi

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@aurorahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora MAP & evaluation timeline - draft

Thanks Rishi — this looks good and aligns with our internal timeline. A few notes from our side:

- We appreciate an evaluation credit for the pilot. Please confirm the size (token-hour equivalent) and whether that credit converts against committed usage.
- Pricing ask: we need clarity on how discounts phase in as we ramp. Aurora will likely increase usage ~3x between pilot and Year 1 target; we want a staged discount tied to commit milestones rather than a flat upfront discount.
- Renewal/expansion: we need an uplift cap and clear triggers. Historically our vendors have applied large uplifts at renewal; can Redwood commit to a maximum uplift band (e.g., no more than +10% YoY on unit price absent changes in product)?
- SLA: what uptime and latency SLOs will apply to the pilot vs. dedicated production?

I’ve copied Daniel from SRE who will help validate the ramp requirements. Also attaching our internal SOW & compliance checklist for the pilot.

Attachments: internal_sow.docx

—Sarah
Sarah Lin
Director, Digital Transformation — Aurora Health
sarah.lin@aurorahealth.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Aurora MAP & evaluation timeline - draft (commercial ask)

Looping you both in for commercial approval and quick guidance. Below is Sarah’s reply — their asks: staged discount tied to ramp, clarity on evaluation credit conversion, and an uplift cap at renewal. They also want SLA differentiation between pilot and production.

My proposed commercial options (short):
1) Conservative (no uplift cap): 10% first-year discount on a 12-month committed volume (min commit $150k), evaluation credit = $10k (applies to first invoice). Renewal pricing determined by market index and usage; legal will push for market-rate adjustments.
2) Balanced (preferred): 12% first-year discount, evaluation credit $8k, explicit renewal uplift cap of +10% YoY on unit price but with a 90-day notice and an exceptions bucket for material product changes. Requires finance sign-off; deal_id RDW-2026-AUR-001.
3) Aggressive (sales-led): 15% first-year discount, evaluation credit $12k, guaranteed no uplift >8% in Year 2 if Aurora signs a 24-month commit and meets ramp milestones. Requires VP approval and a larger upfront commit.

I recommend option 2 as win-win: predictable renewal exposure for Aurora and reasonable protection for Redwood. Also proposing a ramp schedule with three commit checkpoints (pilot -> 50% Year 1 -> 100% Year 1) with pricing bands at each checkpoint. I attached a quick pricing matrix.

Attachments: pricing_options.xlsx

Can you confirm whether legal/finance will accept the +10% renewal cap in option 2? If not, I’ll push option 1 and ask for tighter SLA language to reduce risk.

—Rishi
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Aurora MAP & evaluation timeline - draft (commercial ask)

Rishi — thanks for the summary. Option 2 looks reasonable to me from a commercial/retention perspective. A couple of notes:

- Finance will likely ask to cap the upfront credit to $8k (you already suggested that).
- Legal will review the uplift cap language; if we expose >10% we need a stronger exceptions definition (what constitutes a "material product change").
- If Aurora signs 24 months we can be more aggressive on the discount (apply option 3 approvals).

Please proceed with option 2 and flag in the HubSpot deal record that this requires finance sign-off before sending a bake-off PO. Assign the deal to me as the commercial approver and reference RDW-2026-AUR-001.

Cheers —
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Updated MAP + commercial proposal (option 2)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the quick feedback. Per our internal review we can move forward with the balanced proposal (Option 2). Summary of the updated proposal is below and tracked in the attached MAP v2 and term sheet:

- Pilot: evaluation credit $8,000 (applies to first invoice). Pilot window 3–6 weeks as per MAP.
- Year 1 commit: minimum $150k committed usage; 12% off list unit price applied to committed volume.
- Ramp checkpoints: Pilot acceptance -> 50% commit milestone (30 days post-acceptance) -> 100% commit (90 days post-acceptance). Pricing bands at each checkpoint are in the term sheet.
- Renewal: we will cap standard unit-price uplift at +10% YoY unless there is a documented material product change that reasonably increases cost; such exceptions require prior notice and documented justification.
- SLA: pilot SLA (best-effort) documented in MAP v2; production SLA options available with Dedicated deployment — legal can propose standard SLA attachments.

Attachments: Aurora_MAP_v2.pdf, term_sheet_aurora_20260426.pdf

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of the MAP + term sheet and indicate if Aurora will proceed with annual invoicing and target PO issuance date. Once you confirm, I’ll open the HubSpot deal and route to finance for sign-off (deal RDW-2026-AUR-001).

Thanks and talk soon —
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
